title: India's neighbourhood trade figures: three counterparties do not report at all, and the three that do all record less arriving than India records sending
whatChanged: Nothing changed; the figures never agreed and half of them have no counterpart. For calendar 2024, of the six immediate neighbours other than Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Maldives and Myanmar had filed annual returns with UN Comtrade and Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan had not. Where both sides exist the divergence runs in ONE direction and it is the opposite of the direction a valuation convention produces. India reports exporting US$4.715bn to Sri Lanka against Sri Lanka's US$3.738bn of imports from India; US$0.825bn to Maldives against US$0.502bn; US$0.609bn to Myanmar against US$0.359bn. An importer records CIF and an exporter FOB, so the importer's figure should be the HIGHER one — as it is on every leg of the India-China mirror in P-119. Here it is lower in all three cases, by 26.15, 64.49 and 69.49 per cent of the partner's own figure. No cause is asserted. Candidate mechanisms are partner customs coverage, informal and unrecorded border trade, transit goods recorded as exports on departure and not as imports on arrival, and valuation for duty purposes — none is established by anything retrieved here, and the record says so rather than choosing.
when: Calendar 2024, retrieved 4 August 2026. Non-reporting runs from 2019 for Bangladesh, 2023 for Nepal and 2024 for Bhutan.
bridgeNote:
No reconciliation is published by any party and none is attempted. Both figures are carried where both exist; where only India's exists the record says so rather than presenting a single figure as agreed.

THE THREE ZEROS WERE LOCALISED BEFORE THEY WERE RECORDED, one restriction relaxed at a time. Relaxing the partner from India to the world left all three at zero, so none is an India-specific omission. Relaxing the period is what flips each, at a different year for each: Bhutan 2023, Nepal 2022, Bangladesh 2018. The Bangladesh case was walked back year by year to 2018, where the query returned US$9.409bn — which is both the finding and the positive control that the reporter code and query shape are correct, since a zero produced by a malformed query would have stayed zero at every year.

notes:
Tiered T2 for the reason P-119 gives: these are national submissions retrieved from UN Comtrade rather than from the national customs authorities directly, and the tier grades the document retrieved rather than the institution behind it.

The divergence direction here is the REVERSE of P-119's and that contrast is the point of holding both records. Against China the importer reports more, as the convention predicts; against three neighbours the importer reports less, every time. A single explanation covering both would have to work in opposite directions, which is why none is offered.
